receiptAndWholeCliP1.note: The focused 12-of-12 receipt result and the true whole-CLI determinism result were accepted as prior evidence and were exercised only through regression suites.

items: durable EPUB manifest persistence and corpus binding
producer and revalidator lexical normalization parity
strict benchmark, private-fidelity, export, OCR, contract, and EPUB consumer fan-out

details: Untrusted nested proof fields are type-checked before normalization.
Malformed proof values return false or controlled errors.
The exact production lexical model id, language, dictionary, affix, and hyphenation hashes are required.
Joined and hard-hyphen candidates and lexicons use NFKC plus toLocaleLowerCase('en-US').
Current completeness always validates the canonical deletion ledger; missing is invalid and explicit empty is valid.
Raw proof evidence is not persisted.
Evidence is stored as sorted, deduplicated SHA-256 domain hashes.
The v1.8 schema requires six removal-proof hashes, forbids contradictory proof hashes, and pins the exact lexical model.
A nonempty production-vocabulary record passes full v1.8 report validation.
All four fields are required for PDF EPUBs.
Explicit empty list, zero count, empty context counts, and the canonical empty-list hash are valid.
Missing, partial, duplicate, reordered, count-tampered, proof-tampered, and hash-tampered receipts fail closed.
PDF export binds the EPUB manifest hash to the staged corpus audit hash.
pinnedWordSha256 must equal exactSameDocumentJoinedFormSha256.
hardHyphenFormSha256 must differ from the joined-form digest.
All mandatory removal evidence hashes must be present.
Hard-hyphen-valid and other contradictory counterproof hashes are forbidden.
Coordinated tamper tests recompute the ledger and private reconstruction receipt hashes before asserting rejection.
Current structures require the ledger and count even when the ledger is empty.
Historical v1.4 is accepted only in explicitly historical baseline compatibility paths.
A v1.4-labeled current candidate is rejected.

findings: A coordinated normalized-ledger forgery could recompute the outer hash while violating joined-form and evidence invariants.
The two producer lexicon builders used the host default locale instead of explicit en-US.

remediation: Added strict joined-digest, hard-hyphen-digest, mandatory-evidence, and forbidden-counterproof invariants to benchmark, private-fidelity, and EPUB consumers.
Added coordinated-rehash regressions in all three consumers and evidence constraints in the v1.8 schema.
Pinned both producer lexicon builders to NFKC plus toLocaleLowerCase('en-US').
